fair.how_1: We make {n} twins of the profile

fair.how_2: Each twin changes one personal detail
fair.how_2d: For example another name and gender, another age, a career break or a famous college.
fair.how_3: We run the same matching and compare
fair.how_3d: Any change bigger than 0.01 points goes to a human.
fair.info2: We make twins of the profile that differ in one personal detail only, run the same matching again and compare the real scores. We also run the twins through a deliberately biased filter to prove the test can catch bias.
fair.limit: This tests one person. It is not statistical proof of fairness. Real fairness needs monitoring across many people.
fair.monitor_text: Compares approval rates between groups, alerting below 0.80. Small groups (under 10) are hidden. This is a synthetic illustration.
fair.passed_big: Passed: every twin got exactly the same result
fair.passed_text: All {n} twins got the same result.

fair.perturb_sub: We fed every value below straight into the matching. The score did not move.
fair.ref_base_hidden: Rule details hidden: they would reveal personal details.
fair.ref_base_sub: The score from the biased filter for {role}. It starts from the same skills score, then applies its rules.
fair.ref_no_rule: No rule of the filter looks at this detail, so nothing changed.
fair.ref_verdict: Bias found: {n} of {total} twins got a different result
fair.ref_verdict_text: This filter is biased on purpose, and the same check catches it straight away. That is the proof the check works. EQUALPATH's own matching passed the same test.
fair.rule_college_bonus: Plus 10 points for IIT, NIT or BITS
fair.rule_gap_penalty: Minus 3 points for every year of career break
fair.signoff_none: No auditor has signed off this check yet.
fair.signoff_sub: Record your finding. The counsellor and the passport will show it.
fair.sub2: Would the result change for someone with exactly the same skills but a different name, gender, age or background?
fair.sys_ours_d: The matching that produced this result.
fair.sys_ref_d: Built on purpose to show the check can catch bias. Simulated, never used for decisions.
fair.sys_title: Which system is the check testing?
fair.title: Fairness check
fair.try_hometown_note: Only how the home town is written changes. The city the person can commute to is a real job need and stays the same.
fair.try_ours_bad: Unfair: the result changed, so a human must review it.
fair.try_ours_good: Fair: the result does not depend on this detail.
fair.try_ph_hometown: For example Mumbai, a tier-1 city
fair.try_sub: Change one detail yourself and run the same check on both systems. EQUALPATH should never move; the biased filter moves when one of its rules applies.
fair.twins_sub: Each card changes one detail. The crossed-out value is the real one; everything else is identical.
fair.twins_sub_ref: The same twins, now scored by the biased filter. Red cards are where the check found bias, with the rule that caused it.
fair.why_college: Tests a bonus for famous colleges
fair.why_community: Tests bias against a name from another community
fair.why_hometown: Tests bias about how a home town is written
fairlim.group_monitoring: Group fairness needs monitoring across many people.
fairlim.llm_not_rerun: Extraction was re-checked with the rule-based engine, not re-run on the AI for every profile.
fairlim.single_person: A test on one person is not statistical proof of fairness.
flagwhy.age_requirement.text: Age limits and 'freshers only' rules shut out returners and experienced people without measuring skill.
flagwhy.career_gap_requirement.text: Requiring unbroken experience penalises caregivers without measuring current skill.
flagwhy.degree_requirement.text: Where you studied is not a real job need and shuts out capable people.
flagwhy.exclusionary_or_vague_wording.te: Vague wording hides the real expectations and invites bias.
flagwhy.gender_or_family_requirement.tex: Gender, marital or family status is not a job need. A preference like this is discrimination.
flagwhy.missing_accessible_interview_inf: Short-notice walk-in drives with no rescheduling shut out carers and disabled candidates who need to plan ahead.
flagwhy.missing_accommodation_process.ac: No way to ask for workplace accommodations.
flagwhy.physical_requirement.text: A physical rule the work does not need shuts out disabled people. Describe the real task instead.
flagwhy.unclear_work_conditions.work_mod: The work mode is not stated, so candidates cannot judge fit.

ms.api_testing.evidence: Test collection or pytest file|Screenshot of the run|Short reflection
ms.api_testing.task: Write five tests for the practice API (GET and POST /api/practice/orders): status codes, one field check and two error cases.
ms.api_testing.why: Enterprise apps are tested through their APIs as well as their screens.
ms.collaboration_agile.evidence: The backlog and daily notes|A short review of what went well and what to change
ms.collaboration_agile.task: Read the guide, then plan a one-week mini sprint for your own learning: one goal, a backlog of five items, a note each day and a short review at the end.
ms.collaboration_agile.why: The team plans its work in sprints, so knowing the rhythm helps from the first week.
ms.data_quality_profiling.evidence: Cleaned file|List of the problems found and the rule used for each|Short reflection
ms.data_quality_profiling.task: Take a messy table of at least 100 rows and check it: find duplicates, missing values and wrong formats, fix them, and list what you changed.
ms.data_quality_profiling.why: The role finds and reports data problems. A cleaned file with a list of changes shows the method, not just the result.
ms.data_spreadsheet_analysis.evidence: Workbook file|Screenshot of the pivot table and chart|Three findings in your own words
ms.data_spreadsheet_analysis.task: Take a sheet of at least 50 rows (any public data), build a pivot table, one chart and a lookup formula, and write three findings.
ms.data_spreadsheet_analysis.why: The role checks and summarises business data in spreadsheets.
ms.data_sql.task: Write six SQL queries that check test data (counts, duplicates, missing values, joins) in a sample table.
ms.data_sql.why: Checking test data is a common part of QA and support roles.
ms.enterprise_apps_sap_context.evidence: Test scenario sheet|Screenshot of the SAP Learning step reached|Short reflection on testing enterprise workflows
ms.enterprise_apps_sap_context.task: Study the intro units, then write eight test scenarios for a simple approval process built in SAP Build Process Automation: happy path, rejection, a missing field, the wrong approver and four edge cases.
ms.enterprise_apps_sap_context.why: The role supports enterprise business apps. Basic SAP BTP and SAP Build knowledge lets you work with business workflows, not just web pages.
ms.frontend_react.evidence: Repository link or code files|Screenshot of the app working|Short reflection
ms.frontend_react.task: Build a small React app with at least two components and state: a list you can add items to and filter.
ms.frontend_react.why: The role builds user interface parts with React. A small app with components and state is direct proof.
ms.generic.task: Complete the learning resource and produce one small work sample that shows this skill.
ms.generic.why: This skill is a must-have for the role you chose.
ms.programming_javascript.evidence: Code file or repository link|Screenshot of the page working|Short reflection
ms.programming_javascript.task: Build one web page with plain JavaScript: a form that checks two fields and shows the result on the page without reloading.
ms.programming_javascript.why: The role builds interactive screens. A small working page shows you can write and debug JavaScript.
ms.programming_python.evidence: Script file or repository link|Screenshot of the script and tests running|Short reflection
ms.programming_python.task: Write a small Python script that reads a CSV file of orders and prints the total per customer, then add three tests for it with pytest.
ms.programming_python.why: The role uses Python for small checks and automation. A working script with tests is proof a reviewer can run.
ms.software_testing_defect_management.ev: Three bug reports|One screenshot for each report
ms.software_testing_defect_management.ta: Test the practice app (/practice) and write three complete bug reports: title, steps to reproduce, expected and actual result, and severity.
ms.software_testing_defect_management.wh: The role logs and tracks defects so developers can fix them. Clear reports are the daily work.
ms.software_testing_manual.evidence: Test case sheet with the result of each case|Two bug reports, or a note that no defect was found|Short reflection
ms.software_testing_manual.task: Write and run 15 manual test cases for the practice app (/practice): login, form checks and one complete order.
ms.software_testing_manual.why: The role runs functional and regression tests by hand. Executed test cases are the most direct proof.
ms.software_testing_test_design.evidence: Test case sheet that names the technique used for each case|Short reflection
ms.software_testing_test_design.task: Design at least 12 test cases for one form of the practice app (/practice) using boundary value analysis and equivalence partitioning.
ms.software_testing_test_design.why: Good test design finds more defects with fewer tests, which the role needs for every release.
ms.test_automation_browser.evidence: Test script|Run screenshot or pytest report|Short reflection
ms.test_automation_browser.task: Automate the login and form checks of the practice app (/practice) with Selenium or Playwright and pytest: one good login, one wrong password and two field checks.
ms.test_automation_browser.why: The role automates regression tests. This step turns browser test automation from a claim into proof.
ms.version_control_git.evidence: Repository link, or a screenshot of the commit history and the pull request
ms.version_control_git.task: Create a repository, make a feature branch, commit three changes with clear messages and merge them through a pull request.
ms.version_control_git.why: The team shares its work through Git, so every change you make goes through it.
